finding.summary: Frontend API-keys visibility change has no test at all
finding.evidence: workspace-settings.tsx now (a) renders the API Keys section unconditionally instead of `isOwner &&`, (b) enables the fetchApiKeys query for every member, and (c) adds an owner-only "Created by" column fed by `creatorName(apiKey.createdBy)`. The sole frontend test file for this page (packages/frontend/src/app/workspaces/__tests__/workspace-settings.test.tsx) mocks `fetchApiKeys`/`createApiKey`/`revokeApiKey` (lines 26-28) but never sets a resolved value and never asserts anything about API keys — its three tests cover only member/invite controls. So nothing fails if the section regresses to owner-only, if the query stays disabled for members, or if the Created by column renders for non-owners / maps to the wrong username. This is the user-facing half of the feature and the file already demonstrates the exact owner/non-owner rendering pattern needed.

verdict.reason: The test file contains a dedicated `describe("WorkspaceSettings API keys")` block (lines 222-304) covering every behavior the finding claims is untested. (a) Unconditional section rendering: the test at line 248 renders as a non-owner member and asserts `getByText("API Keys")` (255) and `getByText("Create API Key")` (256), which would fail if workspace-settings.tsx:434 regressed to `isOwner &&`. (b) Query enabled for members: line 254 asserts `fetchApiKeys` was called with "acme" while rendered as a non-owner, the direct inverse of the existing `fetchInvites` not-called assertion at line 190; it would fail if `enabled: !!workspaceId` (workspace-settings.tsx:149) regained an `isOwner` clause. (c) Owner-only "Created by" column and `creatorName` mapping: line 236-242 asserts the columnheader exists for an owner AND that each key row resolves to the correct username (MEMBER_KEY -> "member", OWNER_KEY -> "owner"), while line 258-260 asserts the columnheader is null for a non-owner. The reviewer's cited evidence is also factually wrong against this tree: mocks are at lines 37-39 not 26-28, `renderAs` does set a resolved value via `vi.mocked(fetchApiKeys).mockResolvedValue(keys)` at line 106, and the file has seven tests, not three. Only the network module is mocked; the component's gating logic is real code under test, so this is not over-mocking either.
